meta.title: Arena
meta.subtitle: Site map · roadmap · living document
meta.foundation: Arena is built on top of the existing Launchpad codebase — reusing its working SSO and taxonomy as the base every section below inherits.

statuses.prog: In progress — ETA end of August

sections.name: Launchpad
sections.purpose: The personalized, role-aware home screen — a daily briefing on what needs attention now. KPI cards show Pipeline, Forecast call vs. target with attainment, and training progress; AI-driven panels surface at-risk deals, account plan health, coaching signals (for managers), and high-priority tasks.

sections.name: Revenue Hub
sections.purpose: The numbers side — forecast, pipeline, and account truth for the whole org

items.name: Dashboard
items.desc: The executive revenue hub: a top-down view of quarterly performance combining KPIs, linearity, forward pipeline, and account penetration

children.name: Day 1
children.desc: A single-page executive readout of the quarter combining forecast KPIs, top deals and churn, rotating analytical views (forecast breakdown, area and vertical performance, linearity, Ruby risk).

children.name: ARR Details
children.desc: A sheet-style breakdown of Annual Recurring Revenue across territories and segments.

children.name: Gameboard
children.desc: Account health and whitespace analysis in three sub-views: product Penetration depth within accounts, a strategic account Matrix, and Pen-Traction combining penetration with recent velocity.

children.name: Weekly Cadence Dash
children.desc: A dynamic 13-week pipeline and forecast review dashboard that evolves throughout the quarter, with the weekly view adapting as the quarter moves from pipeline building to execution and close.

items.name: Forecast
items.desc: The sales forecasting hub for the current quarter and beyond: it combines live CRM pipeline with historical patterns and point-in-time snapshots so leaders can call a number, build it bottom-up, judge its risk against history, and explain how it changed week over week.

children.name: Overview
children.desc: The core forecast rollup: a hierarchical territory tree showing pipeline and the calculated "Math Forecast," toggle-able between iARR and Subscription TCV and between Sales and Finance views, with drill-in by territory and a workspace panel for cell-level deal inspection and manual forecast adjustments.

children.name: Build
children.desc: A guided, bottom-up forecast constructor that buckets the quarter into Large Deals, Flow, Large/Small DSC, and Flat Renewals and shows account-level deal tables per bucket — with segment charts, per-deal vs. per-account toggle - with per deal/category adjustments input at AVP and SVP level.

children.name: Linearity
children.desc: Historical quarter-progression curves (1/2/3-year averages) overlaid on the current quarter, with a linearity estimates matrix, run-rate and risk calculations, threshold-based deal assessments, a hierarchical territory filter, and Quarter / Semi-Annual / Annual scopes — answering "given where we are on day N, are we on pace?"

children.name: Bridge
children.desc: Snapshot-to-snapshot or snapshot to live comparison explaining forecast or pipeline movement: waterfall charts of net change decomposed into categories deals between any two snapshot dates, clickable down to the specific deals behind each bar, in either bucket-based or deal-movement views.

items.name: Opportunities
items.desc: A full-featured workspace for exploring and managing opportunities: a sortable, groupable data grid over all deals with dynamic column selection, advanced multi-condition filtering (AND/OR logic), hierarchical territory scoping, keyword search, and configurable summary totals on any amount field. Users can save and share views (columns, filters, sorts, grouping), group records with per-group rollups, inspect any deal in a detail panel and a direct Salesforce link, and export to CSV. Deep-linked from Forecast and Accounts, it serves as the drill-down destination across the app and supports write-back of select fields directly to Salesforce, making it not just an analysis grid but an editing surface for keeping CRM data current.

items.name: Accounts
items.desc: Account truth: list plus per-account deep dive.

children.name: Accounts Overview
children.desc: A high-density account command center that classifies the customer base by pipeline health or account tier, with interactive summary cards showing count, ARR, and current/next-quarter pipeline for each segment. The main table brings everything known about an account into one row across collapsible column groups: ARR/ACV and renewal dates, territory and vertical, the full coverage team (AE, CSM, TAM, SE, partner) with activity levels, services delivery status, product-level ARR breakouts, utilization telemetry (users, robots, consumables), agentic/AI adoption signals, support cases, and forward pipeline — switchable between parent-account (strategic) and child-account (operational) grain. Dedicated tabs extend the view to CS/TAM Coverage, Services, Partners, and Global Accounts. Users can scope by a hierarchical territory filter, drill from any pipeline or ARR figure into the underlying deals, flag key accounts for Big Deal / Day 2 reviews. Accounts can be drilled-down into for the Account Hub view.

children.name: Account Hub
children.desc: The 360-degree single-account workspace: pick any customer and get everything the account team (AE, CSM, TAM, SE, PS/FDE) needs in one place. A persistent header shows ARR, geography, at-risk status, key-account tags, the assigned team, and a renewal countdown with the ARR at stake; tabs then organize the depth — Account Summary (health and key metrics at a glance), Account Data (open pipeline, TCV, product utilization, recent activity, support cases), Account Plan (strategy, interactive org charts, success plans, risk management), Consumption Plan (usage versus targets), Know Your Customer (firmographic and strategic research), and Self-Service reporting.

items.name: Intelligence
items.desc: A centralized section for AI-powered capabilities across the platform

children.name: Conversational Agent on SF Data
children.desc: A conversational Salesforce agent that allows users to query data and perform a limited set of approved updates using their own logged-in credentials.

children.name: Conversational Agent on App Data
children.desc: A conversational Salesforce agent that allows users to query data and perform a limited set of approved updates using their own logged-in credentials.

children.name: Themes
children.desc: A Themes module that analyzes customer interactions across emails and call recordings, identifies recurring topics, concerns, and opportunities, and groups them into actionable themes. Each theme is linked to the relevant accounts, opportunities, and territories, enabling leaders to understand customer sentiment, emerging trends, and common blockers across their organization.

children.name: Support Cases Analysis
children.desc: Analyzes customer support cases to identify recurring issues, trends, sentiment, and escalation risks, then consolidates the findings at account and territory levels to provide visibility into customer health and emerging support patterns.

children.name: Executive Briefing Generator
children.desc: Generates an executive briefing that summarizes performance against quota, current forecast position, pipeline composition, key deal movements, and emerging risks. It highlights the most important gaps, dependencies, and areas requiring leadership attention across the relevant territory or organization.

children.name: Opportunity Insights
children.desc: Generates opportunity-level insights and scoring by analyzing Salesforce fields, historical deal patterns, and recent activity to estimate the likelihood of each deal closing and closing on time. It highlights the signals driving each score, identifies potential risks or gaps, and surfaces the opportunities that require attention.

children.name: Account Insights
children.desc: Generates account-level insights across Account Plan, Know Your Customer, Consumption Plan, and Account Data by combining information captured within the platform, Salesforce records, and recent customer activity from emails, meetings, and call recordings. It summarizes account health, engagement, product adoption, pipeline, risks, and stakeholder coverage, then recommends the next best action for each role on the account team.

items.name: Integrations
items.desc: A section to provide a centralized view of all platform integrations, outlining which systems are connected, how each integration is used, the data exchanged, and the capabilities it enables.

children.name: Salesforce
children.desc: Our CRM backbone, with two connections: a dedicated ingestion pipeline that continuously pulls opportunities, accounts, contracts, support cases, users, and the full sales territory hierarchy; and per-user OAuth for secure write-back, so select field updates made in the app are written to Salesforce under the user's own identity and permissions. The ingested data drives virtually everything: the Forecast module (Overview, Build, Bridge), the Opportunities workspace, account views, and territory-based filtering and access control throughout the app.

children.name: EDW
children.desc: Our enterprise data warehouse feed. We pull finance-grade data that goes beyond CRM: ARR history, ultimate-parent account rollups, and curated account/opportunity records. This is what powers ARR figures on the Dashboard and Ruby Accounts, customer-360 views in Account Hub, and any analysis that needs official revenue numbers rather than pipeline estimates.

children.name: Snowflake
children.desc: We pull utilization telemetry (users, robots, consumables, deployment types) and agentic/AI adoption signals (agent runs, Maestro runs, trends) from Snowflake. This data is surfaced in the Utilization and Agentic Signal columns on Ruby Accounts and in Account Hub's product utilization views, showing how deeply each customer is actually using the platform.

children.name: Exchange
children.desc: Email and calendar intelligence. We pull message and meeting activity from mapped mailboxes to build account activity and opportunity timelines (who's been meeting and emailing whom).

children.name: Tribble
children.desc: Tribble powers the app's AI capabilities, working in context, surfaced through the in-app assistant to answer questions, generate insights and perform updates

children.name: Clari CoPilot
children.desc: We pull recorded customer calls (Zoom/Teams/Meet) with participants, transcripts, and topics, and generate AI-written structured summaries of each call. Surfaced as call history and summaries on accounts and opportunities, giving teams searchable context on every customer conversation.

children.name: FDE App
children.desc: We pull engagement scores, project milestones and blockers, and engineer utilization from the FDE Sentinel system. Surfaced in the FDE columns on Ruby Accounts and engagement-health views, showing where field engineers are deployed and how those engagements are progressing.

children.name: Slack
children.desc: We sync account-linked Slack channels and their recent messages, matching channels to Salesforce accounts, and surface that discussion in account views. The integration also works outbound: users can send Slack messages directly from the app, and the app delivers notifications (alerts, task reminders, updates) straight to users in Slack.

items.name: Build Your Number
items.desc: A fiscal-year revenue planning workspace for constructing and pressure-testing your annual Net ARR number from the bottom up.

items.name: My Actions & Alerts
items.desc: A unified work-list combining every task a user owes — commitments captured in account plans alongside system-generated, trigger-driven tasks fired by changes on opportunities and accounts (e.g., risk signals, stale data, or required follow-ups). Each item carries its source, due date, and status, so open and overdue work is tracked in one place instead of scattered across plans and records. It's the action layer of the app: insights and plans become concrete to-dos.
